source_binding: Both complete storage and private-file race suites, policy, package lint, and platform compilation bind all thirteen committed Go files. The source prose check binds the generated storage README and store contract.
limits: The two original regression tests failed because Filesystem did not implement RetainingStore. This proves the absent capability, not a prior deletion defect.

Filesystem now implements explicit generation leases and collection. Current, caller-required generations, and active native leases remain protected. No automatic collection starts. Runtime and object-storage adoption remain incomplete.

The existing publication lock serializes collection, publication, ordinary generation reads, and independent authority-head reads across instances and processes. Each explicit reader owns an independent generation lock. Its idempotent release remains usable after context cancellation.

A bounded scan validates manifests, payload digests, directory identity, optional authority bytes, and known record names before selection. Unknown files, invalid records, missing requirements, stale heads, and incomplete scans refuse deletion. Dry scans do not create generation lock files.

Collection writes a versioned retirement journal before moving the directory. The journal binds its native parent and writer identity, generation identity, access policy, file metadata, and digests. Canonical JSON, exact names, record limits, and trailing-data checks reject unrecognized journals.

The collector atomically moves an expired generation to a retired directory before removing files. It synchronizes directory metadata after removals and removes the journal last. A pass that fails reports only completed deletions.

Recovery cancels preparations that never moved the source, so a later reader or pin can protect it. Recovery resumes partial deletion only for remaining files that match their recorded receipts. Unknown or changed retired content, a replaced writer, or a replaced parent prevents cleanup.

Retirement journals use the existing recoverable private-record publisher under generations/.record-publications. Collection recovers its owned staging first. Scan counts include metadata. Capacity totals count encoded manifests and payloads but exclude locks, journals, and filesystem overhead.

Tests cover four subprocess exit points, a reader in another process, independent lease lifetimes, ordinary-read exclusion, concurrent publication, new requirements after interrupted preparation, dry runs, scan limits, malformed journals, replaced files, unknown files, and replaced writers or directories.
Both complete package suites pass 250 test events, including parents, without failures or skips. The suites repeat the same cases on two Go toolchains. They do not supply 500 distinct cases.

The first lint check found two new collector diagnostics and five existing private-publication diagnostics. Small concept-owned functions preserve journal parsing, stage writes, and publication outcomes. A platform-specific file now owns the Linux/Windows ACL bound. Final lint and goago pass without policy changes or suppressions. The intermediate receiver-name diagnostic remains preserved.
The source prose check passes. Linux and Windows test binaries compile. These macOS tests do not qualify native Linux or Windows filesystem behavior.

The earlier clean c8ec797a runtime/storage command passed 1111 test events with two skips because the public catalog fixture was absent. This result predates both retention changes. Prepare that fixture before final runtime qualification.

Object-storage retention, runtime adoption, observation-file collection, distinct-inventory retirement, twelve mapped subcases, full verification, review, native CI, and merge remain open. CSP5 remains unpublished until its complete contract passes.
Five concurrent tooling edits remain outside this commit. Final task qualification must use the committed module graph.
The final canonical prose check passes. Source snapshots separate the concurrent tooling edits from six owned documentation files. Task criteria, scope, invariants, and the goal remain unchanged.
The first canonical prose check found seven sentence, paragraph, and phrasing diagnostics. The final check passes after preserving the facts and revising their wording. Both checks remain archived.
